tagline: A mill community, a memorial chapel and an arsenal behind road names.
intro: Huguenot Trail passes near Fine Creek Mills, a community established at the creek’s lower falls, while the Huguenot Memorial Chapel occupies a wooded site off Route 711. Closer to Richmond, Old Gun Road takes its name from Bellona’s arsenal and foundry on the James River’s south shore.

The Huguenot road name reflects an organized memorial effort. The Virginia chapter of the Society of the Founders of Manakin successfully petitioned the General Assembly to name the old River Road “Huguenot Highway.” By 1935, the society had secured land beside the church for a monument to the French Protestant refugees who settled at Manakin in 1700. The monument was erected in 1936 and dedicated in 1937.

For a west-to-east sequence, begin with the mill district near Huguenot Trail, then the memorial chapel off Route 711, and finish with Bellona’s history at Old Gun Road. The arsenal site lies off Route 673 northwest of its junction with VA 147.

moments.title: Fine Creek Mills
moments.text: A gristmill established in the 1730s helped form the community at Fine Creek’s lower falls. A road beside the creek led to the James River ferry at Lee’s Landing, connecting the mills to the river and railroad to Richmond. The community remained a commercial center into the mid-20th century, with a school, store and post office. The historic district includes mill ruins, the Fine Creek Manor site and a miller’s house dating from the mid-18th century. An early-20th-century school, store and gatehouse associated with cheese production also belong to the district, alongside the older milling remains.

moments.title: Huguenot Memorial Chapel
moments.text: The chapel’s pointed windows and three-sided entrance belong to an 1895 church, the fourth building to serve King William Parish. Older materials complicate that date. In 1985, architectural historians Calder Loth and Edward Chappell confirmed that the building reused parts of earlier structures. Loth raised the possibility that a charred beam came from the second Manakin church, erected circa 1710 and destroyed by fire about 1729. That identification remains a theory, not an established construction date for the chapel. The building moved in 1954 and again in 1985, when it reached land owned by the society preserving it.

moments.title: Bellona Arsenal
moments.text: Old Gun Road’s name comes from two neighboring establishments: Bellona Foundry and Bellona Arsenal. The foundry began in 1810; the Army erected the arsenal in 1816 and began storing the foundry’s cannon there the next year. After the War Department declared the arsenal surplus in 1837, several buildings became a silkworm farm. During the Civil War, the complex manufactured Confederate armaments. Later demolition removed much of the quadrangle. In 1942, C. Merle Luck bought the surviving buildings and began renovations, later converting them into residences. The powder magazine survives without its roof.
